notes: Arduino Due is not in the catalogue, so it is added as a new part type with the header pins used here (2, 3, A0, DAC0, DAC1, 3.3V, GND.x).

The image has no exact hole coordinates. Breadboard columns and rows are chosen to match the layout: the pot is in the top half (columns 15-17), button 1 spans the centre gap at columns 20/22, and button 2 at columns 26/28. The topology follows the manual and image.
The top and bottom rail pairs are bridged by long red (power, tp-bp) and black (ground, tn-bn) wires. The rails carry 3.3V and GND from the Due.
Each button has side 1 on the pin column (blue wire from pin 2 or 3 on top, 10K pull-down to the ground rail below). Side 2 goes to the 3.3V rail by a red wire.
Pot: one outer leg to 3.3V, the other to GND, wiper to A0 by the yellow wire. The outer pot leg's side is arbitrary because the pot is symmetric.
DAC0 and DAC1 are outputs only, to an optional oscilloscope. They are not wired, because the oscilloscope is optional and not in the image.
The USB cable and power supply for the Due are not shown in the image and are omitted.
